title: Launch window choreography: staggered feature lanes and dependency fallback protocol
creator: Carlos Nguyen
description:
Goal: Define and validate a repeatable, low-friction choreography for coordinated launches that span the Runtime, Console, and API surfaces. The choreography must support staggered feature lanes, clear dependency gates, and automated fallback behavior so product teams can ship model/runtime changes without cascading outages.

Background: Over the last three quarters we've seen near-miss incidents where concurrent launches across runtime (kernel/kernel-selection changes), console (rollout UI), and API (route / model alias updates) created resource contention and inconsistent user experience. Existing playbooks are fragmented by team and assume manual coordination. This ticket scopes a single cross-team protocol ("Launch Window Choreography") with templates, signal definitions, and automation hooks.

Success criteria:
- A documented playbook (Confluence) that all three teams agree to and can follow for any release touching Runtime/Console/API.
- Automation recipes (CI/CD gating, feature-flag windows, and capacity reservation API calls) implemented as scripts or GitHub actions for the top 3 launch classes (minor patch, model variant swap, major runtime kernel change).
- Defined observability dashboard (dashboard link below) with SLO/cost/traffic signals and escalation thresholds.
- One pilot rollout using the choreography (target: runtime-1.19 canary) completed with postmortem and improvement actions.

Out-of-scope: full company-wide launch calendar enforcement; we will integrate later once playbook is approved by the Release Council.

High-level approach:
1) Launch slot model - timeboxed slots (2h/4h/24h) with lane types: quickpatch, canary-wave, and ramp. Slot owner coordinates cross-team cutovers and publishes preflight checklist 48h in advance.
2) Staggered lanes - schedule Console UI changes in earlier lanes to allow product rollbacks before runtime/backend changes hit production.
3) Dependency gating - explicit preconditions (capacity reservation success, synthetic canary pass, schema compatibility check) must be met before next lane opens.
4) Fallback protocol - when a gate fails, automated rollback to previous model/runtime variant or temporary routing to "degraded" prediction lane is executed and notifications are sent to on-call and PMs.
5) Telemetry and escalation - dashboards with latency, error budget burn rate, token-cost spike, and model quality regressions feed into a three-tier escalation policy.

Primary owners/stakeholders:
- PM lead: Maya Patel (assignee)
- Runtime engineering owner: Priya Shah (ENG)
